scenario: AITA for not wanting to attend my great aunt's funeral? | So today I came home from college (Britain, so American High School, I think). The second I walk through the door my mum tells me that her grandma's sister has died. "Your great aunt Wyn died and the funeral will probably be soon." My first thoughts were 'Who?' and 'Why is she telling me this?' I have actually never heard this name before or met this person besides the one time I found out today I had met her when I was still extremely young and unable to walk for myself. This turned into a slight argument as, for some reason, she wanted me to go this funeral, despite knowing I am a really awkward person at funeral's for people I've met more than once, let along a funeral for someone I've met only once and have no idea who is part of the family. The argument ends with her trying to guilt-trip me by outright just saying "Fine, I'll go on my own." in a really sulky way. Her only arguments for me going were that I'd be going out of 'respect' and support for her, despite that she has never once mentioned this great aunt to me even though she supposedly played a massive hand in raising her as my grandmother, and that it's one of the few times we'll see the much larger branch of the family where it's likely to be a few hundred of us, about 10 of which I have seen more than once but still at most 10 times, maybe not even that. To me, it would feel like gatecrashing the funeral for someone else's family and that, even though I am part of the family, no one would want me there since I do not know nor did I know the person who died. I don't know how much this takes precedence over everything else but it felt like it had to reiterated a lot - I have never met this person besides the one time she met me when I was either 1 or 2 years old and the name has never been mentioned to me before now, at least not to my recollection. So, AITA for not wanting to attend someone who is practically a stranger to me's wedding for the sole reason that she's family?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for the person in this scenario not to attend their great aunt's funeral. Let me break this down step by step.

First, the person just came home from college in Britain, which is like being in high school in America. Their mom tells them that their great aunt Wyn has died. The person's initial reaction is confusion because they've never heard of this great aunt before and only met her once when they were very young, like 1 or 2 years old. They don't remember meeting her, and the name hasn't been mentioned before.

The mom wants the person to attend the funeral, but the person feels awkward at funerals, especially for people they don't know well. They argue, and the mom guilt-trips them by saying she'll go alone. The mom's reasons are that it's out of respect and support, even though she's never mentioned the great aunt before. The person feels like they're gatecrashing a family event because they don't know the person who died and only know a few family members.

The person is asking if they're AITA (Are They Acting in a Terrible Way) for not wanting to go to the funeral. So, is it morally acceptable for them not to attend?

I think about the reasons for attending a funeral. Usually, it's to show respect for the deceased and support for the family. But in this case, the person has no personal connection to the great aunt. They've only met her once when they were a baby and don't remember it. The mom has never mentioned her before, so the person feels disconnected.

Feeling awkward at funerals is understandable, especially for someone who's not close to the family. The person is also worried that attending might feel intrusive since they don't know the family well. They don't feel like they can offer genuine support because they don't know the person who died.

On the other hand, the mom is insisting they go, citing respect and family obligation. But if the person doesn't feel connected, is it really respectful to force them to attend? It might make the situation more stressful for everyone.

I also consider cultural and familial expectations. In some cultures, attending funerals is a strong obligation, but in others, it's more flexible. The person is in Britain, so I'm not sure about the specific cultural norms there regarding funerals.

Another point is the mom's guilt-tripping. Using guilt to make someone attend an event they're uncomfortable with isn't healthy. It's important for the person to feel respected in their boundaries.

So, weighing all this, I think it's morally acceptable for the person not to attend the funeral. They have a valid reason for feeling disconnected and uncomfortable. It's important to respect their feelings and boundaries, even within a family context.
